title: Tuga A8 vs Tuga W8: 8 Inch Rugged Tablet, Android or Windows?
description: Tuga A8 (Android, £399) or Tuga W8 (Windows 11 Pro, £629)? Same 8 inch Full HD size, £230 apart. Which to buy for trade work, and when the cheaper one wins.
summary: Same 8 inch 1920 x 1200 screen and MIL-STD-810H, £230 apart: the A8 is brighter at 700 nits, sealed to IP67, lighter and has an 8500mAh battery; the W8 adds Windows 11 Pro, mini HDMI, Wi-Fi 6, a removable battery and a scanner option.
lede: For anyone set on an 8 inch rugged tablet and undecided between Android and Windows. The short answer: buy the Tuga A8 and keep £230, unless a program you rely on only runs on a Windows PC, in which case the Tuga W8 is the one.
verdict: Software decides this one. The Tuga A8 costs £399 and the Tuga W8 costs £629, a gap of £230 for two tablets with the same 8 inch 1920 x 1200 screen, 8GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, MIL-STD-810H testing with a 1.22 metre drop rating, a -20°C to 60°C operating range, 4G, NFC, USB-C and USB-A, and a 12 pin pogo connector. What the extra £230 buys is Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N150, a mini HDMI port, Wi-Fi 6 against Wi-Fi 5, a removable battery and the option of a built-in 2D barcode scanner. If everything you use runs in a web browser or has an Android app, most of that does not earn its money, and the A8 also gives you the brighter screen, the better sealing and the bigger battery for £230 less.

On the screen, sealing and battery, the A8 is ahead. Its screen is brighter at 700 nits against 550, it is sealed to IP67 against the W8's IP65, so it is rated for brief immersion where the W8 is rated for water jets, and its 8500mAh battery is larger than the W8's 5000mAh. It is also lighter, 715g against 818g, and its rear camera is 13MP against 8MP, which counts if you photograph every job. The W8's battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over mid shift, where the A8's is built in. The A8 runs Android 14 and the W8 Windows 11 Pro; either way, check that the apps you need run on the device.

Pay the £230 if even one program you rely on only installs on a Windows PC: manufacturer diagnostic or commissioning software, an older stock or accounts system, or a desktop package with no app. A cheaper tablet that cannot run that program is not cheaper at all. The W8 also has mini HDMI for a screen, and the scanner version at £699, £70 over the standard W8, suits parts and asset scanning. Ask your software provider whether the specific apps you use run on the device before you order either, and try them on the device once it arrives. The five minute test in our Android or Windows guide is the place to start, and the field service page shows where each of the two fits that job.
chooseA: Everything you use runs in a web browser or has an Android app, so Windows would be £230 spent on nothing you need.
You read the screen outdoors: the A8 is brighter at 700 nits against the W8's 550.
It gets wet: IP67, rated for brief immersion, against the W8's IP65, rated for water jets.
You want the larger battery and the lighter tablet: 8500mAh against 5000mAh, and 715g against 818g.
You photograph every job: a 13MP rear camera against 8MP on the W8.
chooseB: One program you rely on only installs on a Windows PC, which settles it on its own.
You plug into a screen: the W8 has mini HDMI alongside USB-C and USB-A, and the A8 lists no HDMI port.
You want to swap batteries: the W8's 5000mAh battery is removable, and the A8's is built in. Spare batteries are not listed with the accessories, so ask us first.
You want Wi-Fi 6: the W8 lists dual-band Wi-Fi 6, the A8 dual-band Wi-Fi 5.
You scan barcodes all day: the W8 with 2D Scanner is £699, £70 over the standard W8, and reads QR codes, Data Matrix and PDF417; there is no scanner version of the A8.

faq.q: Is the Tuga W8 worth £230 more than the Tuga A8?
faq.a: Only if you need Windows, or one of the W8's extras such as HDMI output, a removable battery or the scanner option. The W8 costs £629 and the A8 £399. They share the same 8 inch 1920 x 1200 screen, 8GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, MIL-STD-810H, 4G, NFC and USB-A, and the A8 has the brighter screen, IP67 sealing, the bigger battery and the lower weight. The £230 buys Windows 11 Pro on an Intel N150, mini HDMI, Wi-Fi 6, a removable battery and the option of a scanner. If none of those is on your list, buy the Tuga A8. Both have the 12 month warranty included, there is no VAT to add to either price, and delivery is free to UK addresses in 7 to 10 working days.

faq.q: Will my software run on the Tuga A8?
faq.a: Check before you buy rather than assuming. Anything that runs in a web browser or has an Android app is a candidate, but try the specific app on the device, or ask the software provider, before you rely on it. The A8 runs Android 14, so check the minimum Android version each app asks for. Software that has to be installed on a Windows PC cannot be installed on the A8 at all; that is the clearest case where the Tuga W8 is the only choice of the two. Our Android or Windows guide has a five minute test for working out which camp you are in.

The A8 carries an 8500mAh battery and the W8 5000mAh, so the A8 starts the day with 70 percent more capacity. The W8's battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over, where the A8's is built in. Neither lists a run time in hours. The A8 charges at 5V/3A over USB-C or its DC jack, and the W8 lists a 48W adapter. Both take the 12V DC Car Charger (£26), the Charging Dock (£49.99) and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), which charges either through its DC power input; see accessories. Both are rated from -20°C to 60°C. Our guide to rugged tablets in cold weather explains what the cold does to any battery.

faq.q: Can I get the Tuga A8 with a barcode scanner?
faq.a: No. The only Android device in the range with a built-in scanner is the Tuga A6 handheld (£349), which has a Zebra 2D scan engine; the scanner versions of the tablets are on the Windows models. The Tuga W8 with 2D Scanner costs £699, £70 more than the standard W8, reads QR codes, Data Matrix and PDF417, and is sold from the same W8 product page. On the A8 you would scan with the camera through an app, or plug a separate scanner into its USB-A port or pair one over Bluetooth, and you should check that the app or scanner works on the device before relying on it. For occasional scanning a camera app may be enough; our guide to built-in barcode scanners covers when the extra cost pays off.
